text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj told a cabinet meeting Moroccan economy indicators evolved positively.
- Interior Minister Driss Basri to visit Madrid next month to discuss issues related to clandestine immigration.
- Recognition of self-styled Saharan Arab Democratic Republic (SADR) was a political mistake, said Congo's Prime Minister.
- Moroccan press union concerned by dispute over Anoual newspaper suspension.
- Government officials and trade union leaders hold first meeting after the 'gentleman's agreement'.
- After the referendum, debate of political parties to concentrate on elections.
- Opposition Istiqlal party leader M'hamed Boucetta calls for a government of transition to prepare 'credible and transparent general elections' in 1997.
- Morocco's 10,000-metre world record holder, Salah Hissou, celebrates his victory, in home town of Kasba Tadla.
- Algeria softens its position on Western Sahara dispute. Paper says Polisario movement is finished.
- With continuing political changes, right-wing Moroccan parties are expected to join the opposition.
